findings.reason: the plan has acted on exactly this edge three times already (§44→§45, §49→§44/§45); leaving s51 unordered reintroduces the concurrent-writer defect the dispatch queue exists to prevent.
findings.text: §51 is `implementable`, absent from `plan-section-depends-on`, and writes `reckon/crew/plan_review.py`, the module §45 also writes while itself `implementable`, so a batch can launch both against one file with nothing ordering them

findings.reason: the test as specified and the base-revision negative control assert different outcomes, so a worker may keep the disjunction, watch the first branch pass at base, and close the node with the reported collision untouched.
findings.text: the done-when accepts "Either the second returns the first's run id, or each writes only its own report directory", but at the reviewed revision a second compose for a plan whose review is still live already answers `dispatched: false, review_run_id: <standing>` (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:2443-2447` and `:2450-2453` at ea4fefcd4, via `_standing_plan_review`), so the first branch is satisfied by the unfixed base and cannot fail

findings.reason: either the colliding write is on a path that does not read the record's own run id, which the repair must name, or the negative control cannot reproduce and the node has no failing base arm against which to score its fix.
findings.text: the section's endpoint and negative control assume a base revision "where one run's report lands in the other's directory", yet each compose mints a fresh run id (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py:412`, `runs.new_run_id`) and the report directory is keyed on that id (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:4967`, `review_report_directory(project, plan_slug, run_id)`), so two composes with distinct ids cannot collide through that resolution and the section names no locus where they could

findings.reason: a brief composed from this section can hand a worker a file to create, inviting a second module that duplicates the existing composer instead of repairing it.
findings.text: the write path reads "`reckon/crew/review_compose.py` or the module composing plan reviews", and no such file exists at the reviewed revision (the composer is `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py`), so the first-named target resolves to nothing

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §51's first write path, `reckon/crew/review_compose.py`, does not exist at the reviewed revision, and its fallback ("the module composing plan reviews") names nothing a batch reader can resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §51's done-when admits "the second returns the first's run id" as an acceptable outcome, and that branch already holds at the plan's own base revision, so the test can pass on unfixed code.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §51 requires every log under the run directory with its revision, literal command and a final `EXIT=` line, which is durable and re-openable.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §51 carries no plan labels, ticket numbers or changelog prose into code; `stored: true` and `review_run_id` are behaviour, not identifiers.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the section offers "refused or returns the existing run" as an already-implemented behaviour and the report-directory isolation as an equal alternative, so the node's verdict can be earned by the branch its own evidence shows cannot fix the reported collision.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §51 names one deliverable (each composed plan review writes only its own report directory); the two admissible outcomes are a done-when defect, recorded there.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §51 declares no `plan-section-depends-on` entry although it writes `reckon/crew/plan_review.py`, which §45 also writes and §45 is still `implementable`.
